transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I came in because I’m kind of at the point where I can’t stop thinking about this area right here—around my jaw and down into my neck. It just looks sagging to me, and uneven, like one side hangs different or catches the light wrong. I know people tell me it looks normal, and I’ve had people say, “I don’t even know what you’re talking about,” but that almost makes me feel worse, because I still see it every time I look.

And it’s not just when I’m looking in the mirror at home. When I’m at work, or around families and nurses, or even at church, I feel like that’s the first thing people notice when they look at me. Like they’re looking right at my neck or my jawline, even if they don’t say anything. I keep trying to tell myself maybe I’m making too much of it, but it feels so obvious to me, and I’m just really tired of it being in my head all the time.
Do you find yourself similarly preoccupied with other parts of your body, or is your main concern specifically with your jaw and neck area?

It’s mainly that area, the jaw and neck. I mean, I might have little things I don’t like like anybody does, but this is the thing I can’t seem to leave alone in my mind. It’s that sagging, uneven spot—at least that’s how it looks to me—right along here, under the jaw and down the neck.

And I know people say it looks normal. My family has said they don’t see what I’m talking about, and I’ve had people kind of brush it off like, “No, you look fine,” but when I’m around families at work, or nurses, or people at church, I feel like that’s what they notice first when they look at me. Like their eyes go there, even if they’re trying not to. So yes, it’s mostly that. That’s the part I keep getting stuck on.
